_synthetic: Synthetic: fabricated for the Dexter's Lab review-pipeline example. Not from a real review.
summary: A one-page note describing the Drip Pool, a constant-product two-token pool with a derived 'pressure' signal p = a/b used for faucet payouts. The central result is a closed-form pressure update law after a swap. The note also claims round-trip neutrality under zero fees and asserts that all identities are machine-checked.

claims.statement: Pressure is defined as p = a/b over the pool reserves.
A swap of da units of A into the pool preserves a*b = k and pays out -db = b*da/(a+da).
After a swap of da units of A in, the new pressure is p' = p*(a+da)/a.
With zero fees, a round-trip swap (da in, received amount back) returns the trader exactly to their starting balances.
All identities in the note are machine-checked.

results_audit: The note has derivations for D2, a proof sketch plus one worked numerical example for D3, and prose assertions for D4 and D5. No simulations, no data, no cost analysis, no artifact for the machine-checking claim.
notable: The D3 proof is a one-line 'by construction' sketch; the worked example (a=100, b=100, da=25, p'=1.25) is the only evidence.
Claim D5 names no proof assistant and links no artifact.
The limitations section concedes no fees, no concurrency, no gas, but does not mention oracle or external-price questions.
